pagina.entradilla: In the Sierra Morena, on the Vía de la Plata and at the gateway to Extremadura: a land of dehesa pasture, Iberian ham and painters.
pagina.descripcion: History, heritage, festivals and food of Monesterio (Badajoz, Spain).

historia: The Vía de la Plata has run through Monesterio for two thousand years. In Roman times the town was called Curiga: this is attested by an inscription, now in the Centro de Interpretación de los Caminos Jacobeos (the Santiago pilgrim routes interpretation centre), and by the Roman columns, ashlar blocks and cornices on the façade of the church.
After the capture of Montemolín, around 1247, the area passed to the Order of Santiago, which held it until 1875. By the 14th century Monesterio was already an encomienda of the Order.

Around 1573 the Crown separated it from the Order and sold it to Seville. In 1632 the banker Octavio Centurión was named Marquis of Monesterio: the chequered band on the coat of arms comes from his lineage.
The town grew in the 19th and 20th centuries around the main road, with its inns. The dehesa of holm oaks and cork oaks, of about 16,000 hectares, and the Iberian pig industry are now its engine.

Iglesia de San Pedro Apóstol.texto: From the 15th century, with Roman remains on the façade, an altarpiece of 1639 and the processional cross by Francisco de Alfaro (1597).
Iglesia de San Pedro Apóstol.alt: An old black-and-white photograph: a cobbled street with the church tower at the end

Museo del Jamón.texto: Opened in 2012 at the entrance to the town from Seville. It tells the story of the dehesa, the Iberian pig and the traditional pig slaughter (matanza); it ends in a courtyard with the dehesa in miniature.

Museo Micológico.texto: The first in Extremadura, in the old grain silo: three rooms on the fungi and mushrooms of Tentudía.
Museo Micológico.alt: The white tower of the old silo among palm trees, at sunset

Pilar de la Reverencia.texto: A granite drinking trough from 1911, right in the middle of the main road through the town. A witness to a century of travellers.
Pilar de la Reverencia.alt: A granite drinking trough topped with a pyramid, among white houses

Paseo de Extremadura.texto: The old N-630, the road of the Vía de la Plata, which splits the town in two and brings together shops and hostels.
Paseo de Extremadura.alt: The main road with whitewashed houses on both sides and a stormy sky

Cocedero de Altramuces de La Cabra.nombre: Cocedero de Altramuces de La Cabra (lupin-cooking site)
Cocedero de Altramuces de La Cabra.texto: A Site of Cultural Interest since 2012: vegetable garden, water wheel, ponds and a lupin-cooking site from the early 20th century, on the Calera de León road.

Monasterio de Tentudía.texto: In the municipality of Calera de León, 10 km along the Ruta de Tentudía. The Virgen de Tentudía is the patron saint of Monesterio.
Monasterio de Tentudía.alt: A battlemented stone monastery on a meadow, under a blue sky

Iglesia de San Pedro Apóstol.detalle: First mentioned in the 15th century. Rib vaulting over the high altar, a Mannerist altarpiece by Jerónimo Velázquez (1639), an 18th-century Rosary chapel and paintings by Eduardo Acosta. Open to visit during Mass times.

Ermita de la Virgen de Tentudía.nombre: Chapel of the Virgen de Tentudía
Ermita de la Virgen de Tentudía.detalle: In a former warehouse of the La Cruz del Pilar flour mill (1906); a place of worship since the 1960s, restored in 1999. Open to visit during Mass times.

Cocedero de Altramuces de La Cabra.nombre: Cocedero de Altramuces de La Cabra (lupin-cooking site)
Cocedero de Altramuces de La Cabra.detalle: A Site of Cultural Interest and Place of Ethnological Interest (Decree 68/2012). Vegetable garden, water wheel, channel, ponds, lupin-cooking site and gardener's house, at km 3.25 of the Calera de León road.

Dolmen de La Cabra.detalle: A passage grave more than 5,000 years old, with a mound 22 metres across, beside the Vereda de la Plata. Nearby are another megalith at La Cabra Baja and a Visigothic tomb at Hoya Montuosa.

Castillo de las Torres.detalle: The ruins of a late medieval fortified house with three round towers, beside the Camino de la Plata and the border with Andalusia.

Las cinco cruces.detalle: Those of El Barrio, El Puerto, La Candelaria, the Gorda or de la Trocha, and El Llano. Those of El Barrio and El Puerto reuse Roman stones.

Pilares y abrevaderos.detalle: The Pilar de la Reverencia (1911), the Pilar Viejo, the oldest, and the granite Pilar del Llano.

El Mojón.detalle: A native sport: two teams of six throw «rebolos», rounded stones, to knock down the opposing team's mojón, a wooden block about 50 cm tall.

Romería de San Isidro.nombre: Pilgrimage of San Isidro (Romería de San Isidro)
Romería de San Isidro.cuando: From 15 May, for several days, in the Pradera del Culebrín

Concurso de Cortadores de Jamón.cuando: August, in the Plaza del Pueblo

Feria del Emigrante.nombre: Feria del Emigrante (fair for those who left the town)

Romería de la Virgen de Tentudía.nombre: Pilgrimage of the Virgen de Tentudía

Feria y Fiestas y Día del Jamón.nombre: Fair, Festivals and Ham Day (Feria y Fiestas y Día del Jamón)
Feria y Fiestas y Día del Jamón.cuando: Around 8 September; Ham Day is on the second Saturday. Festival of Tourist Interest in Extremadura

platos: Revoltillos con morcilla lustre (scrambled eggs with blood sausage)
Patatas con espinazo (potatoes with pork backbone)
Sopas de tomate con higos (tomato soup with figs)
Arroz con conejo o liebre (rice with rabbit or hare)
Guarrito frito o en caldereta (young pig, fried or stewed)

Eduardo Naranjo.texto: A painter of magic realism. Medalla de Extremadura (Extremadura Medal) in 1991. His «Cerdo universal» is in the Museo del Jamón.

Eduardo Acosta.texto: A painter and teacher of painters, among them Eduardo Naranjo. He decorated the dome of the church's Sagrario (tabernacle chapel) in the 1940s.

Isabel Márquez.texto: A native of Monesterio and the mother of the painter Francisco de Zurbarán.

Diego Muñoz Naranjo.texto: A resident of Monesterio who accompanied Zurbarán to the Court and worked with him in the Salón de Reinos of the Buen Retiro (1634).

Camino de Santiago: El Real de la Jara –.nombre: Camino de Santiago: El Real de la Jara to Monesterio
Camino de Santiago: El Real de la Jara –.resumen: A 19.6 km stage along the Vía de la Plata: the Castillo de las Torres, the Culebrín stream, the chapel of San Isidro and the climb to the Cruz del Puerto.

Ruta de Tentudía.resumen: From the Museo del Jamón to the Monastery of Tentudía: 10 km, medium difficulty.

Ruta Aguafría – Castillo.resumen: To the Aguafría summit (1,079 m) and the Castillo viewpoint: 12.5 km, medium difficulty.

Ruta del Camping.resumen: Past the El Cerezo industrial estate, the Cruz del Puerto and the Culebrín stream: 9.5 km, low difficulty.

Ruta de Montemolín.resumen: A path to the neighbouring town. Route sheet as a PDF.

Ruta de Calera de León.resumen: A path to the neighbouring town. Route sheet as a PDF.
